items.statement: Structure and thermochemical meaning of the first H-loss channel
items.expected: Establish the supported first regioisomeric H-loss product as a neutral-singlet six-membered adjacent-Si/N heterocycle with the 4-methyl connectivity corresponding to P1, and interpret its actual product-plus-H thermochemistry. Mapped geometry, bonding and electronic-state evidence must identify the product; a name or empirical formula alone is insufficient. Calculate the atom-balanced 0 K E0=electronic energy+ZPVE relative to separated neutral-doublet SiN and neutral-singlet isoprene, including the neutral-doublet H coproduct, and explain whether and how the resulting exothermic channel is compatible with the measured −162±27 kJ/mol observation. Preserve the full 15-atom/59-electron doublet total inventory. Neither the source −156 value nor the experimental interval is a numerical pass window; assess actual physical compatibility, method limitations and any discrepancy. A copied interval, an unbalanced reaction, a 298 K solution Gibbs substitution or an unsupported product label fails. This is a product/channel conclusion, not proof that its formation route or branching has been established.

items.statement: Structure and thermochemical meaning of the second H-loss channel
items.expected: Establish the distinct second regioisomeric H-loss product as the neutral-singlet six-membered adjacent-Si/N heterocycle with the 5-methyl connectivity corresponding to P2, and interpret its actual product-plus-H thermochemistry. Use independently mapped product structure/state evidence; relabelling P1 does not establish a second candidate. Compare its atom-balanced 0 K electronic-plus-ZPVE channel energy, including neutral-doublet H, with the same separated SiN+isoprene reference and the measured −162±27 kJ/mol observation. Explain the physical exothermicity and compatibility or discrepancy; the source −150 and the measured interval are evidence, not scalar acceptance windows. Keep the complete 15-atom/59-electron total doublet inventory, and distinguish this product/channel claim from a demonstrated formation route or branching ratio. No complete second formation network is required.

items.statement: A physically connected formation explanation for the H-loss product family
items.expected: Explain how the separated SiN/isoprene reactants can form a supported methyl-substituted adjacent-Si/N cyclic product and eliminate H under the stated single-collision conditions. The reference connected P1 route supports terminal N-addition, cyclization and hydrogen rearrangement followed by Si–H loss, but these labels, individual author intermediates, order of shifts, number of saddles and particular IRC algorithm are not scoring requirements. An independently demonstrated chemically equivalent route passes. Actual graph/state-consistent connections from intact reactants to product+H and energies relative to the same reactants must substantiate the claimed formation account; an energy-compatible endpoint or copied reaction sketch alone fails. Assess reachability against the collision energy, distinguishing local barriers from total energy heights. No complete P2 network is required.

items.statement: What the observed energy and finite formation evidence identify
items.expected: Conclude that the two computed product asymptotes are consistent with the observed H-loss channel, while the energy interval alone cannot distinguish their branching or exclude every unsearched isomer. Distinguish the product family supported by structural/energy calculations from the product for which a connected formation route is actually demonstrated. Use the actual overlap and finite route coverage to explain the unresolved alternatives; do not infer equilibrium fractions, exclusive products, universal infinite-distance barrierlessness or interstellar rates.
